newsitem.title: UK: Doctor to examine nurses charged with Saudi murder.
newsitem.headline: Doctor to examine nurses charged with Saudi murder.

text.p: Saudi authorities have agreed to allow an independent doctor to examine two British nurses awaiting a Saudi court verdict in a murder trial, a Foreign Office spokesman said on Monday.
He said this followed British pressure for something to be done about the conditions in which Deborah Parry, 38, and Lucille McLauchlin, 31, were being kept in jail.

Parry and McLauchlin are charged with murdering 55-year-old Australian nurse Yvonne Gilford whose body was found in her room at the King Fahd military medical complex in the eastern Saudi city of Dhahran in December.

They face possible execution if found guilty since the dead nurse's brother, Frank Gilford, has repeatedly called for the death sentence and Saudi law gives the victim's family the right to ask for this.

Despite British press reports speculating that a guilty verdict has already been decided in the case, the spokesman said: "There are no reports from the Saudi authorities that a decision has yet been reached."
He said Britain had been pressing for some time for something to be done about the conditions in which the nurses are detained.
"One suggestion was that the two nurses be seen by an independent British doctor...the Saudi authorities have now agreed to this," he said.
He said the British embassy in Riyadh would now be arranging for this to be done as soon as possible.
Parry and McLauchlin say they are innocent of the murder of Gilford, who was stabbed 13 times, bludgeoned and suffocated, and have withdrawn confessions they said were made under duress.
If they are found guilty, the case is expected to go through an elaborate appeals system.
Saudi Arabia applies strict Islamic laws including beheading by the sword for murderers, drug smugglers and rapists.
